notes: Tagged neutral because the net effect on the SI4 regime cannot honestly be called yet. Watch for the task and finish group, the consultation on regulatory changes, and whether the 170kg limit survives. NRW is directly involved through the enforcement funding. Corroborated 2026-07-20 from the farming side: NFU Cymru (31 March 2025) is 'frustrated' that the review response changed nothing material and continues to press to loosen the 170kg limit and closed periods; a Senedd bid to scrap the rules failed; the 2022 High Court challenge was dismissed. So the regulations have held (the supportive reading for SI4) under sustained pressure to weaken them. Multiple independent sources now, hence reinforced and confidence high; direction stays neutral because the review could still loosen them.
summary: Written statement of 8 October 2025: the independently chaired statutory review completed in March 2025 and Ministers will take all 23 recommendations forward in full and at pace. The direction for SI4 is genuinely two-way: alternatives to the closed periods and the 170kg nitrogen limit are being explored, which could loosen the core controls, while civil sanctions are being considered and 1.58 million pounds was committed for NRW enforcement in 2025-26, which strengthens them. Any substantive regulatory change goes to formal consultation.
title: Control of Agricultural Pollution Regulations review: all 23 recommendations taken forward, alternatives to the 170kg limit on the table
